lines.trans: Senior, are you not heading home?
I have to write an incident report—you guys head home first.
Goodbye, and thank you for your hard work!
Although proper nouns such as place names must be double-checked multiple times…
of all nights, the producer who pulled an all-nighter could not fight off sleepiness and missed it.
Just then, the writer in charge missed it while taking a sip of coffee.
And the flickering final-edit ceiling light left unfixed for six months acted up worse than ever that day.
In the end, everyone's reasons and excuses piled up and overlapped into an accident.
As the main producer of this program, I feel a heavy sense of responsibility.
What comes after an accident is what really matters—so what am I supposed to do next?

meanings.note: Someone who started earlier than you.

examples.trans: school senior
My senior bought me a meal.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.
I want to went inside right now.
How about trying to went inside together tomorrow?
I have to write an incident report—you guys head home first.
Here the word for 'written incident report' is key.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.en: first, before others, ahead of time
meanings.note: Indicates priority in order or time.

examples.trans: It's late, so I'll head in first.
Who arrived first?

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?
Goodbye, and thank you for your hard work!
This expression comes from 'keep up the hard work!'.

examples.text: 지명 등의 고유명사는 여러 번 확인을 해야 함에도 불구하고,
examples.trans: Although proper nouns such as place names must be double-checked multiple times…
Here the word for 'place names' is key.

examples.text: 지명 등의 고유명사는 여러 번 확인을 해야 함에도 불구하고,

examples.text: 지명 등의 고유명사는 여러 번 확인을 해야 함에도 불구하고,
examples.trans: Although proper nouns such as place names must be double-checked multiple times…
Here the word for 'proper nouns' is key.
Did you hear about this several?
I was busy today because of several.

meanings.note: Follows native Korean numbers (한 번, 두 번, 세 번) to count how many times.

examples.trans: I watched this movie three times.
Please explain it just one more time.

examples.text: 게임을 하기 전에 미리 확인을 받으라고? 지금 장난해?
examples.trans: Get approval in advance before every game? Are you kidding me right now?
The topic of confirmation, approval came up during this shoot.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

examples.text: 지명 등의 고유명사는 여러 번 확인을 해야 함에도 불구하고,
examples.trans: Although proper nouns such as place names must be double-checked multiple times…
This expression comes from 'notwithstanding'.

examples.text: 사고라는 건 하필이 세 번이면 일어난다.
examples.trans: An accident happens whenever three bad coincidences line up in a row.
Here the word for 'unlucky timing' is key.

examples.text: 하필 전날 밤을 샜던 담당 PD는 졸음을 이기지 못해 확인하지 못했고,
examples.trans: of all nights, the producer who pulled an all-nighter could not fight off sleepiness and missed it.
Here the word for 'the night before' is key.

examples.text: 여기가 바로 편집실이다, 앞으로 네가 가장 많은 밤을 새우게 될 곳이지.
examples.trans: This right here is the editing room—the place where you will pull the most all-nighters from now on.
Here the word for 'nights' is key.

examples.text: 하필 전날 밤을 샜던 담당 PD는 졸음을 이기지 못해 확인하지 못했고,
examples.trans: of all nights, the producer who pulled an all-nighter could not fight off sleepiness and missed it.
This expression comes from 'stayed up all night'.
Her assigned producer? That pancake guy from last time?
Here the word for 'in charge, assigned' is key.

meanings.note: Hangul spelling of the English abbreviation PD, widely used in Korean broadcasting.

examples.trans: Who is the PD in charge of the new program?

examples.text: 그녀는 예능 피디가 되기 위해 시험을 준비했다.
examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

examples.text: 하필 전날 밤을 샜던 담당 PD는 졸음을 이기지 못해 확인하지 못했고,
examples.trans: of all nights, the producer who pulled an all-nighter could not fight off sleepiness and missed it.

examples.trans: of all nights, the producer who pulled an all-nighter could not fight off sleepiness and missed it.
This expression comes from 'overcome'.

meanings.en: to be unable to, cannot do
meanings.note: Expresses inability; follows a noun in 말 못하다 (cannot say).

examples.trans: I cannot swim.
I couldn't contact you because I was busy.
Let's checked together today.
I worked hard to checked yesterday too.

examples.text: 원래 연예인 하려다 작가 되신 거 아니에요?
examples.trans: Didn't you originally prepare to become a celebrity before becoming a writer?
Everyone does say I don't look like a typical writer.

examples.text: 커피 시킬 때 보면 돼요, 이름 긴 거 시키는 사람들 있거든.
examples.trans: Just watch when they order coffee—some people order drinks with super long names.
Here the word for 'coffee' is key.
I want to drink right now.
How about trying to drink together tomorrow?

examples.trans: Did she never act cranky toward you even once?
This expression comes from 'did she vent?'.
In the end, it all comes down to a battle of nerve and momentum.
Here the word for 'in the end' is key.
Yes, let's each head to our own separate homes, senior!
Here the word for 'each person's own' is key.

meanings.note: Used when explaining why something happened.

examples.trans: What is the reason you are late?
There is no special reason.

examples.text: 결국 각자의 이유들과 변명들이 쌓이고 겹쳐 사고가 발생했고,

examples.trans: A big traffic accident happened on the road.

examples.text: 조심하지 않으면 사고가 날 수 있어요.
examples.trans: If you are not careful, an accident can happen.

meanings.note: demonstrative determiner placed before a noun

examples.text: 이 바닥은 자기 밥그릇은 자기가 챙겨야 돼.
examples.trans: In this industry, you have to look after your own rice bowl.
This book is interesting.

meanings.note: software or planned sequence of events

examples.trans: There are many fun variety shows these days.
I am planning a new show.

meanings.note: loanword from English 'producer', often abbreviated as PD (피디) in Korea

examples.trans: Seung-chan is a rookie producer at a broadcasting station.
Who is the producer of that variety show?

examples.text: 네가 회식 가면 본인이 뭐가 되냐고.
examples.trans: She asked what that would make her look like if you showed up at the dinner.
Here the word for 'she herself' is key.

examples.text: 제가 입도 무겁고요, 얘기 듣는 것도 좋아합니다.
examples.trans: My lips are sealed, and I really enjoy listening too.
This expression comes from 'is heavy (tight-lipped), and'.

examples.text: 이 프로그램의 프로듀서인 본인은 무거운 책임감을 느낍니다.
examples.trans: As the main producer of this program, I feel a heavy sense of responsibility.
Here the word for 'sense of responsibility' is key.

examples.text: 지난번도 느낀 건데 너 누구한테 연애를 가르치니?
examples.trans: I noticed this last time too—who do you think you are lecturing about romance?

examples.text: 이번 일은 꼭 잘 해결해 봐요, 느끼다는 마음으로요.
examples.trans: Let's make sure we handle this well (felt, noticed).

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: refers to something known to both speakers or near the listener

examples.trans: That movie was really fun.
What is that person's name?
Let's meet next time.
The next station is Seoul Station.
Health is the most important thing.
There is an important meeting today.
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?
